newsitem.title: PERU: Lima stocks end up again on miners' lead.
newsitem.headline: Lima stocks end up again on miners' lead.

text.p: Continued strong rises in the mining sector Wednesday pushed up the Lima Stock Exchange for its seventh consecutive rise, brokers said.
The blue-chip index closed up 0.57 percent at 2,719.07 points, while the general index gained 0.26 percent to 1,858.94 points, according to preliminary figures from the market.
Brokers said zinc price rises and mining companies' healthy growth prospects were behind the sector's spurt.
"It is estimated that the price of zinc will advance more, so the prices the mining stocks show at the moment are sustainable and could increase," said Bruno Calle, of Argenta brokerage.
A total 41.5 million soles ($15.7 million) was traded Wednesday in 2,329 transactions.
Miner Morococha soared 10.2 percent to 4.43 soles, while another miner, Perubar gained 10.04 percent to 5.48 soles, and Minsur was up 1.96 soles to 10.90 soles.
Benchmark Telefonica del Peru lost ground Wednesday, closing off 0.76 percent to 6.55 soles.
Overall, 33 stocks ended lower, while 31 were flat and 27 saw gains.
Market analysts said industrial stocks were suffering a lean period, except those related to construction.
